body:
### Summary

## Context
I'm running a monorepo with multiple packages which depend on each other.
I deleted a package by its directory before uninstalling it using uv. I then deleted the reference to the dependency in the pyproject.toml. 
This reulted in a situation where the `uv.lock` keeps a record of the local dependency, but the dependency is not in the expected local directory.

## Expected Behaviour
Any dependency that cannot be found can be deleted so as to refresh the configuration and establish a working state (and potentially reinstall the dependency).

## Actual Behaviour
The dependency cannot be found or deleted through the command line, and must be deleted manually through editing generated files.

## Proposal
- A uv sync / lock doctor comand should trace the problem and provide broad, but applicable advise.
- uv remove should remove broken dependencies (with a warning and prompt if deemed necessary)
- uv lock commands should handle edge cases involving `uv.lock` file.

Thank you for your time and contributions. Python development was not accessible to me until UV changed the monorepo and library development stories. I deeply appreciate this project.

### Platform

macOS 26 Tahoe (Intel CPU)

### Version

uv 0.11.28 (Homebrew 2026-07-07 x86_64-apple-darwin)

### Python version

python 3.12
title: uv sync fails on missing dependency which cannot be removed
